title: Twilight rays at La Silla
caption: Twilight and star trails over La Silla Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at La Silla Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: ESO Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: The last rays of sunlight paint a blend of orange, red and yellow near the horizon at ESO's La Silla Observatory, but the bright star trails curving through the sky steal the show. Each trail marks the path of a single star, recorded over a long exposure. Below, the rear lights of moving vehicles leave their own trails, tracing the region's network of roads.

ESO Photo Ambassador Roger Wesson made the picture by combining 763 separate 20-second exposures. He began approximately 40 minutes after sunset and kept going through the night, so that both the fading twilight and the lengthening star trails appear in one image.
Sunset is when the observatory's staff can get down to their real work of studying and exploring the night sky. ESO's first observatory, La Silla remains among the most productive in the world.

understand.summary: This is a composite of 763 exposures of 20 seconds each by Roger Wesson, spanning twilight and the night. The source does not publish camera or colour-processing details.
understand.eye: No observer could see twilight and hours of star motion at once. The combined exposures place them together in a single frame.

alt: Curving star trails over an observatory, with orange, red and yellow twilight at the horizon and vehicle light trails along roads below.
